reaction.episode: DIGESTION episode through the October 23 close (data fresh, not stale): SPX at 7623.68 is 2.82% below its 120-day high, 0.99% below its 50-day (7699.64) and 4.56% above its 200-day (7291.31); SMH at 527.20 is 21.53% below its high and sits BETWEEN zones, NVDA at 210.96 sits just ABOVE Zone 1 (200-210); VIX is 19.45, HY OAS is 3.23 and calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is only 1 of 4 (credit calm alone).

reaction.trapRisk: Both SPX (7623.68) and SMH (527.20) sit below their failure zones (7750-7820 and 580-600), so any bounce toward those bands is guilty until proven innocent: the pivot-and-fail pattern means the first bounce is the trap, not the entry. Entries change accordingly — no chasing a bounce into the failure zone, no adding on a single green day; a probe requires either a Zone 2 washout print or a held close above the failure zone, and a rejection at the zone confirms the trap and keeps capital on the sidelines.

strategyPosture: Watch through the October 28 FOMC: the digestion is real but unconfirmed as a bottom (mechanical tally 1 of 4, SMH between zones), credit is calm enough to hold but not to add broadly, and the best setups (semis, selective power) are staged at Zone 2 prints, not chased on bounces.

themes.counterRead: The divergence itself is the risk: if credit flips from loose to cracking, a rotation becomes a rollover fast. The position that respects both readings is to treat index-level calm as permission to be selective, not as permission to add broadly — the weakness is concentrated in the names that dominate the index, so single-name selection matters more than index direction right now.
themes.dataAnchor: The concentration read is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER: Mag7 names average 13.99% below their 52-week highs against SPY at 2.8%, an 11.19-point divergence gap, with AAPL the strongest at 1.1% below its high and TSLA the weakest at 25.4%. The episode block agrees: SPX is only 2.82% below its 120-day high (7844.52) while SMH is 21.53% below its own. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold), which is what keeps this a rotation read rather than a confirmed broad rollover.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — index calm masks Mag7 weakness
themes.narrative: The market read is that the tape is calm: SPY is only 0.79% off over the past month and sits 2.8% below its 52-week high, so the drawdown looks contained.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS breaking above 4% or SLOOS tightening toward the 40% stress zone would void the rotation read and reframe this as a rollover.

themes.counterRead: Oversold does not mean bottomed: SMH is between zones (527.20, below Zone 1 at 540-565 and above Zone 2 at 470-505) with a 20-day return of -13.08%, and the mechanical capitulation tally is only 1 of 4. The data says these are the names to own eventually; the tape says the washout is not confirmed over. That gap is exactly why entries here are staged (probe at Zone 2, add only on confirmation) rather than chased on the first green day.
themes.dataAnchor: The dislocation list is deep and broad: AMAT 49% below its high (RSI 26.1) with revenue growing 11.4% YoY, LRCX 47.5% below (RSI 24.6) with revenue growing 131.3% YoY, KLAC 52.6% below (RSI 23.3), ONTO 48.6% below (RSI 26.5) with revenue growing 22.1% YoY, and AVGO 35% below (RSI 34.2) with revenue growing 55% YoY, 67.8% gross margin and a 42.1% FCF margin. NVDA, the conviction promotion at score 83, is 13.3% below its peak with revenue growing 61.4% YoY. These are multiple-compression and sentiment-driven declines, not broken-revenue declines.
themes.label: Semiconductor washout — prices derated while revenues still grow
themes.narrative: The market read is that the AI hardware trade is broken: semis have been sold for a month straight and sit 35-50% below their highs.
themes.watchFor: SMH closing inside Zone 2 (470-505) or NVDA inside Zone 1 (200-210) would mark the washout reaching a buy zone; a mechanical tally rising to 3 of 4 would confirm capitulation.

themes.counterRead: This is a derating of a story that ran ahead of delivery, not a verdict that the theme is dead — insider buying at the VST trough and BWXT's growth argue the power buildout continues, just at lower multiples. The distinction matters for positioning: BWXT-type names (growth intact) are hold-and-stage candidates, while VST-type names (deteriorating revenue) need the insider signal to be confirmed by a revenue turn before they earn new money.
themes.dataAnchor: The one-month laggard list is dominated by the power complex: SMR -37.19%, OKLO -31.26%, URA -16.37%, GEV -14.87% and PWR -15.31%, with BWXT 47.4% below its high and VST 31.2% below its high. But the fundamentals are split, not uniformly broken: BWXT revenue is growing 26.1% YoY (watchlist promotion, score 77) while VST's revenue inflection reads DETERIORATING even as insiders bought $1.17M at its trough (watchlist promotion, score 78).
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power — the story ran ahead, now derating
themes.narrative: The market read through the summer was that nuclear and AI power demand was a one-way structural trade; the past month says otherwise.
themes.watchFor: VST revenue inflection turning from DETERIORATING to recovery, or BWXT closing back above its 50-day, would mark the derating as overdone.

themes.counterRead: Leadership on the way down does not guarantee leadership on the way back: leveraged structures reset through volatility decay and forced selling, so a bounce in these names is the least trustworthy signal in the tape. They are the last place to probe for a bottom, not the first — confirmation must come from the unlevered complex (SMH/NVDA zones) before any crypto-beta name earns a probe.
themes.dataAnchor: The one-month tape confirms it: CONL -34.28% (down another 5.72% today), ETH-USD -13.61% (down 2.64% today), COIN -17.53% (down 2.84% today) and held name BMNR -20.05% over the month. These are the steepest beta-adjusted declines in the tracked set, and they are leading, not following, the broader digestion — SPY is only 0.79% off over the same month.
themes.label: Leveraged crypto beta leads the drawdown
themes.narrative: The market read is that crypto-linked leverage is unwinding first and fastest, as it usually does when risk appetite cools.
themes.watchFor: A held SMH close back above its 50-day (575.09) with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 would be the earliest permission to even look at crypto-beta probes.

themes.counterRead: Calm credit plus an elevated VIX is a stable-but-fragile combination: it supports holding through the digestion, but it also means the FOMC print can reprice both rates and equities at once. The 10-year sitting at 4.99, essentially on 5%, is the level where a hot print would turn digestion into something worse — the posture into the meeting is patience, not prediction.
themes.dataAnchor: Credit is not the constraint right now: HY OAS is 3.23 and reads calm, the 2s10s curve is positive at +0.22 (2Y 4.77, 10Y 4.99), breakeven inflation is 2.35 and the real 10-year is 2.64. VIX at 19.45 is elevated (22% above its 50-day average of 15.94, and the 5-day high) but has not spiked and is not rolling over — consistent with digestion, not panic. The FOMC event carries HIGH signal strength with 3 matched headlines, and the December 8-9 meeting is already anticipated at HIGH.
themes.label: Rates and credit calm into the October 28 FOMC
themes.narrative: The market read is that the Fed meeting on October 27-28 is the next real catalyst, with inflation still the swing factor after the hotter-than-expected September CPI print (active event, HIGH signal).
themes.watchFor: The October 28 FOMC decision and any 10-year close sustained above 5.00% would reprice the digestion; a 10-year settling back under 4.90% with HY OAS still under 4% would confirm calm.
